transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

My thoughts feel all jumbled and I can’t keep my words or plans straight anymore, even for simple tasks I’ve done for years. It's gotten to the point where I just can't seem to manage my daily routine, and I'm really struggling.
Did this confusion come on suddenly over hours or days and does it go up and down during the day, or has it been building slowly over months? Also, are you having trouble staying focused or alert?

It didn't happen overnight; it has been building up slowly for over a year now, ever since my husband's health got worse. I also have a terrible time staying focused because the smallest things, like a squeaking cart or a flickering light, will completely pull my attention away. Before I know it, I've wandered off and completely forgotten what I was doing or trying to say.

Have you been seeing or hearing things that others don’t, or strongly believing things others say aren’t true? If so, did those experiences start after any medical illness, head injury, seizure, or new medication?

Yes, I hear a man's voice telling me I'm failing my husband, and I truly believe my boss and the hospital are tracking me to judge my caregiving. This didn't start from any head injury, seizure, or new medicine, but rather began and got worse under the heavy stress of taking care of my husband's diabetes complications.

Have you been diagnosed with any brain or memory-related illness, such as dementia, stroke, Parkinson’s disease, or another neurological condition? If so, did your hearing voices and suspicious beliefs start after those problems began?

No, I've never been diagnosed with any neurological conditions like dementia, a stroke, or Parkinson's. These jumbled thoughts and the voices are relatively new experiences for me, and they only started after my husband's health got so bad.

About how long have the voice and the belief that your boss and the hospital are tracking you been present—less than 1 month, 1 to 3 months, or longer than 3 months? Have they been there most days during that time?
It has been going on for almost a year now, so definitely much longer than three months. It happens most days, ever since my husband's hospital stays started piling up.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent psychotic symptoms for nearly a year, including auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, and disorganized thought/speech with marked impairment in daily functioning. The course is chronic rather than fluctuating, and no neurological disorder, head injury, seizure, or medication trigger was identified. This pattern is most consistent with paranoid schizophrenia.
